title: New motor accident injuries (CTP) scheme (ACT)
summary: The ACT's Motor Accident Injuries Act 2019 commenced on 1 February 2020, replacing the fault-based CTP scheme with defined benefits.
direction_rationale: Private insurers already wrote ACT CTP; the reform mainly changed benefits and claims costs, so the competition effect is unclear.
comparison: Victoria and Tasmania keep public monopoly insurers (TAC, MAIB); Queensland has private insurers with regulated premiums

verified.notes: Read on the ACT register: commencement notice CN2019-13.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Replaced the ACT's fault-based compulsory third-party scheme with defined benefits. Fewer disputes over fault cut the legal and claims costs of the scheme; insurers already competed, so the competition effect is small.

marks.reason: Defined benefits reduce the legal and claims-handling costs of fault-based disputes.
